## forest-intact-v01.png

Edit this landscape into ONE clearly defined forest condition for an educational matched-view comparison. Keep EXACTLY the same camera position, perspective, aspect ratio, terrain and rock positions, distant mountain ridge, sky and light direction. Preserve the positions, thicknesses and heights of the major standing tree trunks, especially the big foreground trunk at left, the center slope and the tall trunk at right. No split screen, no new objects, no labels or text, no animals or people. Realistic Sierra Nevada mixed-conifer forest photography. This will be labeled a generated schematic comparison, not observed before/after data. Show the same forest BEFORE the illustrative recent fire: a mature living conifer forest with abundant intact green needle crowns on the standing trees. The foreground and middle-distance trees all have healthy green crowns, the left foreground canopy is full, the understory has shrubs, ferns and leaf litter. Remove visible charring, black fire scars and burned ground. Keep natural gaps between trees; not a solid green wall. Clear visually that canopy and understory are present. Photographic bark and needle detail, balanced exposure, subdued natural colors.
